correctness.rationale: Independent replay from rules alone (stdlib DP to N=8000) confirms every integer: cold list on [0,200] is exactly the 71-entry list; SG distribution (71,71,34,19,6); max nimber 4 at {128,144,160,165,172,200} on [0,200] with sole further 4 at 263; tail max 2 from 264; W[263:270]=[1,1,0,1,0,1,0] and G[264:271]=[2,0,1,0,1,0,1]; 125-length base windows W[263,388) and G[264,389) agree with shift 7; agreement extends to N=8000; residue laws hold; SG=0 coincides with losing globally. Lemma (length-max(S) agreement window implies ultimate periodicity by induction on predecessors) is sound for both W and mex recurrences. Negative certificate (no (q,p) with window>=125 closes inside [0,200]) replays empty. Leastness: W[262]=win vs tail residue lose (262%7=3) rules out every q'<=262 for every period (non-multiples of 7 fail on the infinite 7-cycle tail by gcd argument; multiples of 7 fail at n=262); G[263]=4 vs tail value 1 rules out every q'<=263 analogously; failure of p=1..6 in the tail plus primality of 7 implies no non-multiple period preserves the tail. Draft states leastness tersely (p<7 checks plus last-mismatch witnesses) without spelling the gcd/multiple extension, but the extension is valid and independently verified, so the claims are true as stated. Status is proof (finite certificate + induction), not mere experiment.

Positive controls show the novelty point: A014586 records subtract-a-square Grundy with Rouse Ball/Coxeter, Guy E26, Flammenkamp, Eppstein references (squares only); OEIS 'cube difference free' returns no game/P-set analogue. Eppstein arXiv:1804.06515 abstract and text treat subtract-a-square only (O-tilde(n) winning-set and O-tilde(mn) nim-values, Furstenberg-Sarkozy density, modular structure, nim-values <<|S|). Flammenkamp octal page covers only take-and-break octal rules (0.???, 4.???, 0.0n7, Grundy game), no finite subtraction-cube table. General ultimate-periodicity theorem for finite subtraction sets is textbook background but does not imply the exact numbers (qW=263, qG=264, p=7, cycles, 71-entry cold census, max-4 positions). No prior source records or mechanically implies this cube table.

value.rationale: Headline is a rigorously established exact invariant of a specific natural object: S={1,8,27,64,125} is the complete cube-move set applicable on the range (next cube 216>200), motivated before computation by the recognized square-difference-free/subtraction-periodicity program (Guy E26, Furstenberg-Sarkozy, Eppstein 2018 benchmarks). Values (least preperiods 263/264, least periods 7, cycles, 71-entry cold census with density, SG distribution, max-nimber-4 positions, last-4 at 263/last-3 at 216, proved negative certificate at 200) were not known and are not mechanically implied by squares or octal tables. A future researcher (Eppstein-style solver regression, OEIS anchor, density comparisons, longer cube-truncation studies) could reasonably need this precise row. This is the eligible narrow-invariant case: one exact period/order/census datum with motivated object and non-obvious value. Not a textbook restatement, not a mere parameter substitution of an arbitrary subset, not a tiny unmotivated gain, not an unexplained enumeration.
